target_customer: Patients with chronic conditions such as IBS who pay for app subscriptions, plus healthcare providers who refer them
problem: Drugs do not fully treat gut-brain and other chronic conditions, and clinical hypnotherapy is scarce and costly. Mindset delivers clinically studied hypnotherapy programs through a phone app.
business_model: consumer app subscription plus provider referral programs
product_category: digital therapeutics, hypnotherapy apps (Nerva for IBS, later Evia, Claria, Relio)

founders.name: Chris Naoumidis
founders.background_notes: Brothers per Startup Daily 2021; no background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Pre-recorded hypnotherapy sessions in a mobile app are standard engineering; the hard part is clinical evidence and later AI adaptation.

defensibility.rationale: Content can be copied, but published clinical studies and referral relationships take time to build.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer found; company remains independent per its site.

market_need_then: The founders said in their YC launch post that Nerva already helped 80,000 people manage IBS; the same post cites studies on hypnotherapy for smoking cessation.

identity.logo: wordmark; site uses a Mindovermatter wordmark treatment
identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical credibility: what the brain does, the body feels

branding.brand_signature: Product-level sub-brands such as Nerva for IBS

brand_strength.rationale: Product sub-brands such as Nerva carry the recognition; the company name is generic and no brand press found.

pivots.from: Finito, a self-hypnosis app to quit smoking (YC launch post)
pivots.to: Broader AI therapeutics for IBS and other chronic conditions

outcome_analysis: Mindset Health, founded by two brothers in Melbourne, entered YC S19 with the Nerva IBS app and a smoking cessation launch, raised a 5M seed in 2021 and a 12M Series A in 2023, and now reports 350,000 patients and many provider referrals. It is active, with no exit; the main risks are clinical regulation and distribution.
notes: Competitors left empty: the 2021 seed article names none and no dated rival source was found. Series A details come from search results of two outlets (BioSpectrum Asia, Mobihealthnews; the mobihealthnews page returned 403), not opened directly; company PR Newswire also exists. Earlier small rounds (51,000 USD pre-seed 2018 from Blackbird and Startmate, 150,000 USD YC seed, a 1.1M May 2020 round) appear only in snippets or aggregators and are unverified. Founder backgrounds not found.
